text:
Almost every forecast I am shown uses the planned rate. Very few use the rate we actually achieved.

A simple example:
• Balance: 12,000 inch-dia of welding
• Planned rate: 900 a week. Finish in 13 weeks.
• Achieved rate, last eight weeks: 520 a week. Finish in 23 weeks.

Same balance. Ten weeks apart. And only one of those two rates has ever happened on this site.

The book “How Big Things Get Done” calls this the outside view: look at what really happened on work like yours, not at what you hope will happen.

Three rules I use:
1. Forecast with the rate achieved over the last six to eight weeks.
2. If the plan needs a higher rate, show what changes to get it: crews, work fronts, shifts.
3. Put both dates side by side and let management decide which one to believe.

A forecast built on a rate you have never achieved is not a forecast. It is a wish with a date on it.

Which rate does your forecast use: planned, or achieved?
